summary: Streaming and http.Hijacker behind the enabled response-validation wrap
description:
### Finding (architecture review R1, carried forward from TKT-125)

`shared/go/contract.responseValidated` buffers the response into an `httptest.ResponseRecorder`, which does not implement `http.Flusher` or `http.Hijacker`. No handler behind the wrap can stream or hijack its connection — today, in all five services, whenever response validation is enabled.

### Why TKT-125 split this out rather than fixing it

It is a **policy** decision, not an adapter fix. ADR-028's fail-closed guarantee *requires* withholding the response until the validator has accepted it; a handler that flushed would have already sent bytes the validator might reject. Exposing `Flush` through the recorder would not stream to the client and would break fail-closed ordering. So the real question is which of the two properties a streaming route gives up — and that only needs answering when such a route exists.

Note TKT-125 made this **conditional**: with `OPENAPI_RESPONSE_VALIDATION_ENABLED=false` the handler receives the real `ResponseWriter` and the optional interfaces are restored.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A decision (ADR amendment) on how a streaming route coexists with ADR-028: route-level exclusion, a different validation contract, or streaming stays unsupported
- [ ] If a mechanism is adopted: a test proving fail-closed still holds on non-streaming routes

### Not urgent

No streaming or hijacking route exists in the repo today. This is a placeholder for when one is proposed.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Split from TKT-125 at plan time with a stated justification (draft §4, accepted at plan-review). Not shaped: no DoR, no context-mémo bake — do both before this is Gate-1 eligible.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — NOT promoted (backlog drain, HEAD `ac2952b`)

**Held — no trigger exists.** The ticket says it plainly: "No streaming or hijacking route exists in the repo today. This is a placeholder for when one is proposed." Verified still true. Moving it to Ready would queue a decision about a route that nobody has asked for. Leave it as the tripwire it is.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⏸ HOLD — correctly parked; the trigger still does not exist

Backlog review 2026-08-26 at HEAD `1aaee7cd`. Re-verified rather than inherited.

Mechanism intact: `responseValidated` still buffers into an `httptest.ResponseRecorder` (`shared/go/contract/http.go:118-158`, recorder at `:120-121`, replay at `:153-157`), which implements neither `Flusher` nor `Hijacker`. The doc comment at `:115-117` now states the consequence explicitly. The conditional-on-flag claim holds: `ResponseValidator` returns `next` untouched when validation is off (`:76-78`).

**The ticket's "not urgent" premise is still true.** A repo-wide sweep for `http.Flusher`, `http.Hijacker`, `Hijack()`, `text/event-stream`, `EventSource`, `websocket`, `chunked` and long-poll across Go/TS/Astro/YAML returns exactly one non-test hit: `shared/go/obs/requestlog.go:41-51`, a defensive `Unwrap()`/`Flush()` passthrough in the request-log middleware added at scaffold time — not produced by any route.

**No action.** Both ACs are decisions with no trigger. Leave it as a tripwire; the ticket to re-open it is the first one that proposes a streaming or hijacking route.
